title: ElastiCache for Redis OSS 4 is past end of standard support
summary: AWS ended standard support for ElastiCache for Redis OSS 4 on 2026-01-31. RDS Extended Support may keep it running for a fee through 2029-01-31. Upgrade to Valkey or Redis OSS 7.1 or later.
replacement: Valkey or Redis OSS 7.1 or later

sources.title: Engine versions and upgrading in ElastiCache

constraints: An ElastiCache engine upgrade is an in-place modification; the cache is unavailable while nodes are replaced, and restoring a cluster-mode-disabled cache over a newer engine is not a rollback.
Take a manual backup before the change and verify that it can be restored.
Extended Support keeps the cache running past the end of standard support for a fee; it does not replace moving to Valkey or Redis OSS 7.1 or later.

steps.title: Take a backup
steps.instructions: Take a manual ElastiCache backup of every reported cluster and verify that it can be restored.

steps.title: Upgrade the engine
steps.instructions: Modify the cache cluster or replication group to a supported engine version, or create a new cache on Valkey or Redis OSS 7.1 or later and move clients to it.

steps.title: Raise the declared version
steps.instructions: Change engine_version in every aws_elasticache_cluster and aws_elasticache_replication_group block, Compose service, and Helm value that runs this cache.

steps.title: Check clients and parameter groups
steps.instructions: Update Redis clients, connection strings, and parameter groups that assume the old engine version.

verification.purpose: Review the plan and confirm the engine_version change is intended and is the only cache change.
Confirm any local Compose service that mirrors this cache is valid and uses an image tag that matches Valkey or Redis OSS 7.1 or later.
Confirm each reported cache cluster now reports a supported Redis OSS engine version.
